title: Q4 Launch Campaign Planning
segments: Thanks for joining. The goal today is to agree on the plan for the November launch of our alerting rules feature, including the message, the channels, and who does what.

Quick product context. Alerting rules let customers define conditions like a shipment running two hours late, and notify the right person by email, text, or Slack. It's the most requested feature of the year.
Great. Who's the audience? I'd like to be specific rather than saying everyone.
From the sales side, it's operations managers at mid-sized shippers, the people who currently find out about delays from angry customers. Greg at Northwind is a perfect example.
On the customer success side, I'd add existing customers who haven't turned on any notifications. About a third of our accounts have none configured.
That's useful. So two audiences, new prospects and an adoption push for existing customers. Do we want one message or two?
I'd say one core idea with two framings. The idea is you hear about problems before your customers do.
I like that. It's concrete and it's about the customer's customer. Let me test a headline: Know before they ask.
That's good. It's exactly what prospects tell me on calls.
For the visual direction, I'd avoid generic dashboards. I'd show a single shipment delay and the alert landing on a phone, so the story is one moment, not a feature list.
Agreed. Tom, how long would it take to produce a hero visual and a short product video?
The hero visual is a week. A thirty second video is more like two and a half weeks if we want it to look polished. I'd need the final copy by October fifteenth.
That works. I'll have copy to you by the fourteenth. What channels are we using?
My proposal is a launch email to the full customer list, a blog post with a customer story, LinkedIn posts, and a webinar two weeks after launch.
For the customer story, I can introduce you to two customers who beta tested the feature. One of them cut late-delivery complaints by almost half, and they're happy to be quoted.
That's the proof we need. Can you connect me with them this week?
One concern. The launch is November twelfth, but the SMS alert option depends on a vendor integration that isn't finished. If it slips, we shouldn't advertise it.
Good flag. What's the likelihood it slips?
Maybe thirty percent. I'd say we message email and Slack as the headline, and treat SMS as a bonus if it's ready.
I'll write the copy that way. We can add SMS to the blog post the day it's confirmed.
Can we also give the sales team a one-pager? I have three deals in the next month where this will come up directly.
Yes. I'll draft a one-pager with the pitch, three objection responses, and a demo script. Jenna, can you review it for accuracy?
Sure. If I get it by the twentieth I can use it in two calls the following week.
Done. Now the webinar. I think it should be hands-on, how to set up your first five alert rules, rather than a product pitch. Who should host?
I'd be happy to do the demo part. Priya could join for the customer perspective.
I'd like that. I could also pull together the common rules our beta customers set up so people have a starting point.
Perfect. I'll book the webinar platform for the twenty-sixth of November and open registration at launch.
What about budget? I have about fifteen thousand for the quarter, and I'd like to spend about a third on the video and the rest on promotion.
Would a small paid LinkedIn push to operations titles be worth it? That's where my prospects are.
I think so. Let's put five thousand behind targeted LinkedIn ads for the two weeks after launch and measure demo requests from them.
How will we measure success overall?

Three numbers. Demo requests attributed to the campaign, the share of existing customers who create at least one alert rule within thirty days, and webinar attendance. I'd set a goal of twenty-five percent of the unactivated accounts.
That's ambitious but doable if we run an in-app prompt alongside the email.
Good point. Aisha, can product add an in-app banner pointing people to the rule setup?
I'll ask Sofia to scope it. It should be small. I'll let you know by Monday.
Great. I'll write up the plan and the timeline and send it out today. Thanks all.
overview: Planning session for the November 12 launch of the alerting rules feature. The audience is split between prospective operations managers at mid-sized shippers and existing customers, about a third of whom have no notifications configured. The core message, "Know before they ask," will anchor a launch email, a blog post with a beta customer story, LinkedIn posts, and a hands-on webinar on November 26. Tom will produce a hero visual and a 30-second video from copy due October 14. Because the SMS vendor integration may slip, email and Slack are the headline channels. Budget is about $15k, including $5k for targeted LinkedIn ads. Success will be measured by campaign demo requests, alert rule activation by existing customers (target 25% of unactivated accounts), and webinar attendance.
